text: Differentiate between a finite set and an infinite set, with one example each.
modelAnswer: A finite set has a countable, definite number of elements (its cardinality n(S) is a whole number), e.g. {1,2,3,4,5} has 5 elements. An infinite set has no definite (uncountable) number of elements, e.g. the set of natural numbers N = {1,2,3,...} never terminates.
keyPoints: Finite: cardinality is a fixed natural number
Infinite: cannot list all elements, continues without end
Example each: {days of the week} vs N

text: State the empty-set property of the symbol φ with respect to every set A, and give one example of an empty set.
modelAnswer: φ (the empty/null set) is a subset of every set A, written φ ⊂ A, because the condition 'every element of φ is in A' is vacuously true (φ has no elements to check). Example: {x : x is a natural number, 1 < x < 2} is empty since no natural number lies strictly between 1 and 2.
keyPoints: φ ⊂ A for every set A (vacuous truth)

text: If A = {1,2,3,4}, B = {3,4,5,6}, C = {5,6,7,8}, find A ∪ (B ∩ C) and (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C), and verify they are equal.
modelAnswer: B ∩ C = {5,6}, so A ∪ (B ∩ C) = {1,2,3,4,5,6}. A ∪ B = {1,2,3,4,5,6}, A ∪ C = {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8}; their intersection = {1,2,3,4,5,6}. Both sides equal {1,2,3,4,5,6}, verifying the distributive law A ∪ (B ∩ C) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C).

text: Using Venn diagrams reasoning (describe in words), explain why A − B = A ∩ B′.
modelAnswer: A − B is the set of elements in A that are NOT in B. 'Not in B' is exactly the definition of B′ (complement of B). So an element is in A − B exactly when it is in A AND in B′ simultaneously — which is precisely the definition of A ∩ B′. Hence A − B = A ∩ B′ for any two sets A, B.
keyPoints: A − B means: in A, not in B
'In A and in B′' = A ∩ B′

text: Define 'relation' and 'function' from set A to set B, and state the key difference between them.
modelAnswer: A relation R from A to B is any subset of A × B. A function is a special relation in which every element of A appears as the first element of exactly one ordered pair — i.e. each input has a unique output. The key difference: a relation permits an element of A to relate to zero, one, or many elements of B, while a function requires exactly one image for every element of A.
keyPoints: Function = every element of A has exactly one image
Function is a special, more restrictive kind of relation

text: Find the domain and range of the real function f(x) = √(9 − x²).
modelAnswer: For f(x) to be real, we need 9 − x² ≥ 0, i.e. x² ≤ 9, i.e. −3 ≤ x ≤ 3. So domain = [−3, 3]. As x ranges over [−3,3], x² ranges over [0,9], so 9−x² ranges over [0,9], and its square root ranges over [0,3]. So range = [0, 3].
keyPoints: Need 9 − x² ≥ 0 for a real square root
Max value of √(9−x²) is 3 at x=0, min is 0 at x=±3 (range [0,3])

text: If f(x) = x² and g(x) = 2x+1, find (f/g)(x) and state any value excluded from its domain.
modelAnswer: (f/g)(x) = x² / (2x+1). This is defined for all real x except where the denominator is zero: 2x+1=0 ⟹ x = −1/2, which must be excluded from the domain.
keyPoints: Excluded value: where g(x)=0, i.e. x = −1/2

text: Convert 6 radians into degree measure.
modelAnswer: Degrees = radians × (180/π) = 6 × 180/π = 1080/π ≈ 343.77°, which is 343° 46′ approximately (0.77×60 ≈ 46′).
keyPoints: Convert the decimal part of the degree to minutes: 0.77×60 ≈ 46′

text: Prove that sin(x+y)sin(x−y) = sin²x − sin²y.
modelAnswer: sin(x+y)sin(x−y) = (sinx cosy + cosx siny)(sinx cosy − cosx siny) = sin²x cos²y − cos²x sin²y (difference of squares). Substitute cos²y = 1−sin²y and cos²x = 1−sin²x: = sin²x(1−sin²y) − (1−sin²x)sin²y = sin²x − sin²x sin²y − sin²y + sin²x sin²y = sin²x − sin²y.
keyPoints: Apply sum and difference formulas, multiply as (A+B)(A−B) = A²−B²
Substitute cos² = 1 − sin² for both variables
Simplify — the sin²x sin²y terms cancel, leaving sin²x − sin²y

text: Find the value of cos(−1710°).
Express (1 − i)⁴ in the form a + ib.
modelAnswer: (1−i)² = 1 −2i +i² = 1−2i−1 = −2i. So (1−i)⁴ = (−2i)² = 4i² = −4. In the form a+ib, this is −4 + 0i.

text: Find the multiplicative inverse of 2 − 3i.
modelAnswer: For z = a+ib, the multiplicative inverse is (a−ib)/(a²+b²). Here a=2, b=−3 so a²+b²=4+9=13, and the inverse is (2+3i)/13 = 2/13 + (3/13)i.

text: Solve the quadratic equation x² + 3x + 5 = 0 using the quadratic formula.
modelAnswer: Using x = [−b ± √(b²−4ac)]/2a with a=1,b=3,c=5: discriminant = 9−20 = −11. So x = [−3 ± √(−11)]/2 = [−3 ± i√11]/2, giving two complex conjugate roots.

text: Solve the inequality 2(2x+3) − 10 < 6(x−2), and represent the solution on a number line (describe it).
modelAnswer: 2(2x+3)−10 < 6(x−2) ⟹ 4x+6−10 < 6x−12 ⟹ 4x−4 < 6x−12 ⟹ −4+12 < 6x−4x ⟹ 8 < 2x ⟹ x > 4. On a number line: an open circle at 4, with shading extending to the right (all values greater than 4).
keyPoints: Collect x-terms on one side, constants on the other
x > 4 — open circle at 4, shade rightward

text: How many words, with or without meaning, can be formed using all the letters of the word 'EQUATION', using each letter exactly once?
modelAnswer: EQUATION has 8 distinct letters (E,Q,U,A,T,I,O,N — all different). The number of arrangements is 8! = 40320.
keyPoints: No repeated letters means no division needed

text: A committee of 3 persons is to be formed from a group of 4 men and 2 women. In how many ways can this be done so that the committee has at least one woman?
modelAnswer: Total ways to choose any 3 from 6 people = C(6,3) = 20. Ways with NO woman (all 3 men from the 4 men) = C(4,3) = 4. At least one woman = total − no woman = 20 − 4 = 16.

text: Find the 4th term in the expansion of (x + 2)^5.
modelAnswer: T(r+1) = nCr·x^(n−r)·2^r with n=5. For the 4th term, r=3: T4 = 5C3 · x^2 · 2^3 = 10 · x² · 8 = 80 x².
keyPoints: 4th term means r=3 (since T(r+1) is the (r+1)th term)

text: Find the sum of the first 15 terms of the AP 2, 7, 12, 17, ... .
Insert 3 geometric means between 1 and 256.
modelAnswer: We need a GP: 1, G1, G2, G3, 256 — 5 terms total. So 256 = 1×r⁴, giving r⁴=256, r=4 (taking the positive real root, 4⁴=256). The means are G1=4, G2=16, G3=64.

text: Find the slope of a line which makes an angle of 30° with the positive direction of the x-axis.
modelAnswer: Slope m = tan(θ) where θ is the angle made with the positive x-axis. m = tan(30°) = 1/√3.
keyPoints: Slope = tan of the angle with the positive x-axis

text: Find the equation of the circle with centre (0,2) and radius 2.
modelAnswer: Using (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² with h=0, k=2, r=2: x² + (y−2)² = 4, i.e. x² + y² − 4y + 4 = 4, simplifying to x² + y² − 4y = 0.
keyPoints: Substitute centre and radius into standard form

text: Find the coordinates of the foci and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse 36x² + 4y² = 144.
modelAnswer: Divide by 144: x²/4 + y²/36 = 1, so a²=36 (along y, since 36>4), b²=4. Here the major axis is along y, c² = a²−b² = 36−4 = 32, c=√32=4√2. Foci: (0, ±4√2). Length of latus rectum = 2b²/a = 2(4)/6 = 4/3.
keyPoints: Normalize to standard form: x²/4 + y²/36 = 1
Since 36 > 4, major axis is along the y-axis; c² = a²−b² = 32

text: Evaluate lim(x→0) [(1+x)⁵ − 1]/x.
modelAnswer: This limit matches the standard form lim(x→0) [(1+x)^n − 1]/x = n. Here n=5, so the limit equals 5. (Verification via binomial expansion: (1+x)^5 = 1+5x+10x²+... , so [(1+x)^5−1]/x = 5+10x+..., which → 5 as x→0.)
keyPoints: Recognize the standard limit form [(1+x)ⁿ−1]/x → n as x→0

text: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. Find the probability that it is either a king or a queen.
modelAnswer: Kings and queens are mutually exclusive events (a card can't be both). P(king) = 4/52, P(queen) = 4/52. By the addition rule for mutually exclusive events: P(king or queen) = 4/52 + 4/52 = 8/52 = 2/13.
keyPoints: King and queen are mutually exclusive outcomes
